method: The far-field (Fraunhofer) boundary is r = 2*D^2/lambda and the outer edge of the radiating near field is r = 0.62*sqrt(D^3/lambda), with lambda = c/f and c = 299,792,458 m/s. A measurement distance below 0.62*sqrt(D^3/lambda) is reported as the reactive near field, between the two boundaries as the radiating near field (Fresnel), and at or beyond 2*D^2/lambda as the far field. The largest dimension converts from mm, cm or m, the frequency from MHz or GHz, and the distance from m or km; inputs are limited to 0.001-1,000 m, 1 MHz-300 GHz and 0-1,000 km. Both criteria assume D much larger than lambda and an isolated antenna in free space, so the result is flagged when D is below one wavelength. Ground planes, radomes, nearby metal, array size and pattern-measurement tolerance are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: IEEE Std 145-2013, IEEE Standard for Definitions of Terms for Antennas
